# EasyTier source provenance and local changes

Source: https://github.com/EasyTier/EasyTier
Version: v2.7.1 (prerelease), commit `0d9c52b169dc2112687ddefcf571cd01d383193c`.
Retrieved over HTTPS and independently checked out by Git on 2026-11-17. These are upstream source files, not a reimplementation. This subset includes `easytier`, `easytier-core`, `easytier-proto` and root Cargo metadata/license. GUI/web/FFI and other unrelated workspace members are omitted. Upstream `Cargo.lock` is retained for provenance; the actual adapter resolution is locked in `crates/cyberbus-transport/Cargo.lock`.

License: GNU Lesser General Public License v3 (`LICENSE`, also `easytier/LICENSE`). Copyright notices in sources are retained. CyberBus modifications use the same LGPL terms. Include LGPL and GPL text, corresponding sources/patches and necessary relinkable objects/instructions with static SDK distributions; do not claim an rlib alone satisfies distribution obligations. Upstream repository and original revision remain available above. The incorporated GPL v3 text is included as `GPL-3.0.txt` (GNU text retrieved from GCC mirror `COPYING3`). Dependency versions/licenses (328 unique package/version/source entries across host and Android Cargo metadata) are recorded separately in DEPENDENCIES.tsv; review the actual final application/FFI distribution too.

Local modifications (2026-11-17):

1. Root `Cargo.toml`: restrict workspace members/default-members to these three included crates. Keep shared version declarations unchanged.
2. `easytier/src/instance/factory.rs` and `composition.rs`: add **`create_native_dataplane_instance`**, an opt-in native factory policy. The ordinary upstream factory retains its original behavior. Before both initial normalization and final construction, the opt-in factory sets host `proxy_enabled`, `gateway_enabled`, `force_exit_node`, local exit fallback, portal, magic DNS, UDP broadcast, UPnP to false. This prevents an unbound virtual inbound port from falling through to an OS no-tun proxy even if another dependency enables KCP/QUIC features. No packet format, relay protocol, cryptography, or routing algorithm is changed.
3. `easytier/Cargo.toml`: make the service-manager dependency optional and enable it with `management`, matching its already feature-gated Rust module. It is unused by the embedded transport and should not add desktop service-manager assumptions to Android.

4. Optional WebSocket fallback (2026-11-18): `easytier/Cargo.toml` adds `webpki-roots` to the existing `websocket` feature. `tunnel/websocket.rs` replaces upstream's certificate-verification bypass with public CA and hostname validation; self-signed public WSS origins are rejected. `tunnel/protocol.rs` retains the plain WS positive seam test; self-signed WSS is now covered by a rejection test instead of a success case. Loopback WS origins behind Cloudflare use plain WS internally and validated WSS externally.

Default adapter features remain EasyTier `default-features=false`, `smoltcp`, `aes-gcm`; core `config-write`. No tun/socks5/KCP/QUIC/UPnP/magic-DNS/management/CLI features. Opt-in `cyberbus-transport/websocket` enables upstream WS/WSS transport, not system TUN or proxies; `cloudflared` adds a separately managed official connector process and loopback relay. The SDK enables WS/WSS support while the fallback configuration stays off by default; the Rust connector experiment is archived outside the active build. Host TCP/UDP transport and encrypted EasyTier peer/routing behavior are upstream. The separate public relay runs the unmodified upstream release archive (reports `2.7.1-0d9c52b1-20261115`), not this vendored factory.
